offence_severity: Minimum: 6 months, Maximum: Life imprisonment (Section 304 Part II IPC)
physical_harm: Death due to coma resulting from head injuries caused by blunt weapons
number_of_offences: Five offences charged, three finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence of three eye-witnesses, one of whom was the father of the deceased, and found their presence at the incident to be most natural given the proximity of their shops to the deceased's shop and the time of the incident.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their evidence could not be shaken even in cross-examination and that all three witnesses specifically deposed about the presence of the accused and their individual acts in assaulting the deceased.
bail_history: Accused persons, who are on bail

legal_representation.accused: A. Sharan, Deepak Singh, Rashid Saeed, (for K.S. Rana), Rachana Srivastava, Noorullah, T.N. Singh, Manoj Kumar Mishra (for Kamlendra Mishra)

investigation_status: Accused were arrested barely within 2 or 3 days, post mortem examination conducted, inquest prepared

appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeals dismissed as being without any merit

prosecution_argument: The three appellants alongwith two others formed an unlawful assembly and in pursuance of their common object, committed the murder of PW-1's son by inflicting injuries upon him with lathis/dandas.
defence_argument: There was absolutely no reason for the accused persons to assault the deceased and no motive was attributed to them. The evidence of PW-1, being a father, would be that of an interested witness. The other two witnesses PW-2 and PW-3 were busy in their own shops and could not be eye witnesses. The offences alleged would not come under s.304 Part II IPC and at the most would come under s.325 or s.326 IPC.
legal_principle_applied: Motive in a criminal case is irrelevant where evidence of the eye-witnesses is available.
sentencing_rationale: The punishment imposed upon the appellants is not harsh as alleged. In fact, the punishment is on the lenient side. One young life was lost at the young age of 22 years.
